He will be perceptive of the wonders wrought by God and
he will himself do marvellous things. He hears the command
of Jesus: "Put out into the deep and let down your nets for
a catch." His own deeds appear to him in a new light; they
are no longer the deeds which he has himself chosen to do
and which he accomplishes in his own strength and by his
own planning, they are rather deeds done at God's com-
mand, and hence deeds sustained and completed by divine
grace. In fact he knows that he can dare to do more than
human calculation is able to foresee, for he is independent
of what may be attainable according to human calculations,
and he commits the results of his doing into God's hands.
But his action, flowing from the experienced love of God, is
itself an action inspired by love, and so he has the power to
bear witness to the love of God before others and to embody
God's love in concrete reality. A man whose whole being
and conduct is sustained by the peace and joy of love, is
himself a miracle in the eyes of others. And in this sense we
are all called not only to behold the wonders of God but on
our part to effect wondrous things.
My friends, this is the last academic service of the present
term and it presents usespecially the academic com-
munity which is to-day gathered here—with a serious
question. This term we have been allowed to pursue our
studies in peace, while so many of our fellow-students,
colleagues and friends are at the front, torn from their
normal work, living in stress and danger, and ensuring by
the devotion of their energies and lives the peace of our quiet
round of study. We think of them now in the deep bonds of
fellowship and gratitude. But we must also remember that
for us it is an undeserved grace of God that we have been
able to carry on our work here. Ought we not to interpret
this also as a miracle that has been granted us? Hence let
us shoulder our responsibilities all the more seriously and
bear witness by our own weak action to the mighty working
of God, so that even in these distressing and anxious times the
Creator's praise may ring out. "The Lord's name be praised!"
